name: Today's Report
headline: Renting beats buying by $1,105 a month nationally, and by $5,486 in the San Francisco metro that includes Fremont.

sections.label: Real estate
sections.html:
Today's theme is rent versus buy. Zillow's latest report puts the typical U.S. rent at $1,932 a month in September, while a new buyer's payment, with 10% down and taxes and insurance included, is $3,037. That is $1,105 more every month to own, and rental demand is up 19.2% from a year ago as would-be buyers rent instead.

Here the gap is far wider (chart). In Zillow's San Francisco metro, which includes Oakland, Fremont and Hayward, rent is $3,445 against an $8,931 buyer payment, $5,486 apart. In the San Jose metro, which includes Milpitas, it is $3,812 against $11,845, so the payment would cover the rent three times over. Our two metros also lead the country in rental demand growth: San Jose is up 82.5% from a year ago and San Francisco 66.9%.

The local twist is that rents are rising faster than buyer costs. San Francisco metro rent is up 11.8% in a year while the buyer payment rose 7.1%; nationally it is the other way around. On our own MLS, Fremont's median asking price of $1,300,000 works out to about $8,000 a month in principal and interest alone at today's 7.29% with 10% down, before taxes and insurance.

Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average eased to 7.29% today from 7.35%, and the 15-year is 6.95%, after the Fed held its rate Wednesday (more in Economy). The board wide table is 2,558, from 2,554, with 141 coming soon and 139 brand new. The five city ledger is 670, from 674: Milpitas (103), Newark (89) and Union City (60) held, while Fremont eased to 225 and Hayward to 193.

What this means for you: renting wins month one, nationally and even more so here, so buying is a bet on equity and on staying put. With metro rents climbing about 10% a year, a renter weighing a purchase should compare both paths over five to ten years, not one month. Sellers should know their buyer is often a renter doing exactly that math, so a price that pencils against today's rent gets the call.

  • Board wide: 2,558 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 141 coming soon and 139 brand new.

Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

  • Live ledger: 670 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 601 are on the market and 69 are coming soon.
  • Fremont: 225 live, 179 active, 29 coming soon and 17 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,300,000 at $808 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 35 days.
  • The rest of the ledger: Hayward 193, Milpitas 103, Newark 89, Union City 60.
  • Across all five cities the median is $1,079,000 at $668 a square foot. 282 homes are priced under a million, and 180 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

images.caption: Renting costs $1,105 less a month than buying nationally, $5,486 less in the San Francisco metro and $8,032 less in the San Jose metro, where rental demand rose the most in the country.
images.source: Zillow, Oct. 15, 2026 release and research data (September 2026)

sections.label: Economy
sections.html:
The Fed held. It kept its target range at 3.75% to 4.00% Wednesday, after raising it in September, and two officials, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack, dissented because they wanted another hike. The statement says inflation "remains elevated" and that more information will guide its next step, with the next meeting in December (chart).

The 10-Year Treasury, which mortgage rates follow more closely than the Fed's own rate, closed Wednesday at 5.05%, up from 4.99%, and is near 4.99% this morning. Brent's December contract settled up 1.26% at $115.32, gold rose 0.20% and silver slipped 0.83%. One correction: Market Briefs printed the 10-Year at 4.99% and lower, gold down 0.04% and Brent down 1.07% at $114.07; Treasury's close was 5.05%, gold finished up 0.20% at the 4 PM print, and Brent settled up 1.26%.

images.alt: Step chart of the Fed funds target rate upper bound from January 2025 to October 2026
images.caption: The Fed cut three times in late 2025, held at five straight meetings, raised its rate in September and held again on Oct. 28 at 3.75% to 4.00%.
images.source: Federal Reserve FOMC statements; FRED DFEDTARU

sections.label: Stocks
sections.html:
Alphabet is the story. Its shares are down 13.2% as of 11:23 AM PT, the day after earnings, and the Nasdaq is down 1.59%. Over six months through Wednesday, Microsoft was up 25.1% and Alphabet down 7.3% (chart); today's drop stretches that gap to about 44 points.

Alphabet's top line was strong: revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion and Google Cloud more than doubled, up 103%. What spooked investors was the spending. Capital expenditures hit $51.4 billion in the quarter, more than double a year ago, free cash flow turned negative ($9.1 billion), and earnings per share fell to $2.12 from $2.87, partly on an $8.7 billion loss on stock holdings. Market Briefs said Google's AI sales dipped; the company's release says the opposite. Microsoft's Azure grew 48% on revenue of $92.3 billion, up 19%, and its stock is down 0.35%. Wall Street's message: spend all you like, as long as the cash comes back first.

images.alt: Line chart of Microsoft and Alphabet stock performance from April 29 to October 28, 2026, with Thursday's intraday move after Alphabet's earnings
images.caption: Microsoft rose 25.1% from the Apr. 29 close through Wednesday while Alphabet fell 7.3%. The dashed line is Thursday's trading after Alphabet's earnings, as of 11:05 AM PT.
images.source: Yahoo Finance daily closes (MSFT, GOOG); CNBC intraday

sections.html: Crypto is calm after the Fed. Bitcoin is near $80,800, up 0.06% over 24 hours, Ether is down 0.12% and XRP is down 2.09%, live from CoinGecko at 11:23 AM PT. For once, the coins were steadier than the search engine.
